# jt-demo — Corporate Workstation

The J Toolkit example application: a mid-90s quarterly report dialog
for J Consolidated Industries, Inc., rendered entirely with jt.

* **`jt-demo.exe`** — Windows executable (x86-64). Built by GitHub
  Actions on `windows-latest` from `src/main.rs` and committed here by
  `.github/workflows/build-example.yml`. Just run it; on Windows it
  opens a real window and the checkboxes, radio buttons, region list,
  and OK / Cancel / Help buttons all respond to clicks.
* **`screenshot.png`** — what it looks like, generated by the
  executable itself with `jt-demo --screenshot screenshot.png`
  (headless; the same renderer draws the live window).
* **`src/main.rs`** — the source. The Win32 backend is ~250 lines of
  direct FFI: one window, one `StretchDIBits` per paint, clicks
  forwarded to the app. Everything else is the jt library.

The J does not stand for anything. It is a nice looking glyph.
